anchor: The marble memorial tablets of the Whaleman's Chapel (Seamen's Bethel, New Bedford), which Melville attended in December 1840 and rendered in Moby-Dick ch. 7, set in the engraved small-capitals and modern-face title-page typography of the 1851 Harper & Brothers first American edition (and Bentley's London The Whale)
rationale: Chapter 7 describes the chapel walls lined with black-lettered white marble tablets to men lost at sea, each ending in the chiselled question of whether the dead are in heaven; the corpus is itself an inquiry into whether anything steers the lost. Bone-white marble ground, lampblack lettering, tarnished brass fittings and a Bethel-pew slate accent; engraved capitals for display, Georgia-class modern serif for body.

fonts.display: Copperplate, 'Copperplate Gothic Light', 'Trajan Pro', 'Times New Roman', serif
fonts.body: Georgia, 'Bookman Old Style', 'Times New Roman', serif
